title: Derived tensor-Hom adjunction with a bimodule and retained scalars
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the ordinary module derived categories $D(S),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $E\in D(B)$, $X\in D(B)$, and $V\in D(S)$. Regard $E$ as a $B$-$S$ bimodule by restriction along $S\to B$. Write $J_E(V)\in D(B)$ for derived $S$-linear Hom from $E$ to $V$ with $B$ acting by precomposition: it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for a representative $E^\bullet$ of $E$ and a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $V$, and $(b h)(e)=h(be)$. This is independent of representatives. With $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ the restriction functor, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,J_E(V))\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_S\bigl(U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E),V\bigr).$$
It induces the tensor-Hom adjunction on morphism sets by taking $H^0$, with evaluation as counit. In particular all these comparisons remain compatible with restriction to any ring $K\to S$. No flatness of $B$ over $S$, perfectness of $E$, or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09LN (lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause) and 09LT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); ordinary commutative rings in degree zero, with the S-linear internal-Hom enhancement. The displayed enhancement follows from their chain adjunction using a K-projective B-model of X and a K-injective S-model of V.

proof.text: Work on the one-object site with only the identity and the trivial topology: sheaves of modules over its constant ring $R$ are exactly $R$-modules. Choose complexes $C,E_0,V_0$ representing $X,E,V$. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] choose $V_0\to I$ K-injective over $S$, and by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] choose $q:Q\to E_0$ K-flat over $B$. Put $J=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(Q,I)$, with $(bh)(e)=h(be)$. This action commutes with the Hom differential since $b$ has degree zero. The map $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E_0,I)\to J$ induced by $q$ is $B$-linear and is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] on the one-point $S$-site. The same cited statement applies to quasi-isomorphisms of representatives of $E$ and of K-injective representatives of $V$. Thus $J$ represents precisely the $J_E(V)$ specified in the item, including its $B$-action.

For any $B$-complexes $A,T$ and $S$-complex $N$, use the total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the total Hom of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Define currying, in degree $n$, by
$$\theta(f)(a\otimes t)=f(a)(t):\quad U\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(A,\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(T,N))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_B T),N).$$
It is balanced because $f(ba)(t)=f(a)(bt)$; conversely a balanced map gives $a\mapsto(t\mapsto g(a\otimes t))$. Products on both sides are indexed by all $(p,q)$, so these mutually inverse formulas also work for unbounded complexes. For $a\in A^p$, both differentials evaluate to
$$d_N f(a)(t)-(-1)^{p+n}f(a)(d_Tt)-(-1)^n f(d_Aa)(t).$$
Thus $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $S$-complexes, natural in all variables. This is the explicit elementary verification of the differential graded clause of Tag 09LN, with the source's two algebra names specialized to $B,S$ respectively; no derived assertion is used here.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause and proof hint

proof.text:
The chosen $J$ is K-injective as a $B$-complex. Indeed, for an acyclic $B$-complex $A$, $A\otimes_B Q$ is acyclic by K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Restriction $U$ leaves its abelian groups and differential unchanged, so it is still acyclic over $S$. By Step 2 and the Hom/homotopy identification [lem-sc-module-hom-complex-quotient],
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B)}(A,J)=H^0\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U(A\otimes_B Q),I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(S)}(U(A\otimes_B Q),I)=0.$$
The last equality is exactly the definition of K-injectivity of $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. This proves the required K-injectivity of $J$ by that same definition, without asserting that restriction preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0A96, lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective, proof with the two coefficient rings distinguished

proof.text: The complex $C\otimes_B Q$ represents $X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E$. To check this using the first-variable convention in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], take a K-flat resolution $P\to C$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. That cited functor statement identifies $P\otimes_B E_0$ with the derived tensor and says that $P\otimes_B Q\to P\otimes_B E_0$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Also $P\otimes_B Q\to C\otimes_B Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the K-flatness of $Q$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Hence the resulting zigzag identifies $C\otimes_B Q$ with the required tensor. Step 3 and [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identify $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(C,J)$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,J_E(V))$. The same definition over $S$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U(C\otimes_B Q),I)$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E),V)$. Localizing $\theta$ of Step 2 now gives the displayed isomorphism in $D(S)$.

source.place: Tag 08J9, lemma-internal-hom, proof; mixed-ring analogue using dga.tex Tag 09LN and more-algebra.tex Tag 06Y6

proof.text: The isomorphism is canonical and natural. On complexes its component is the formula of Step 2; precomposition in $C$ or $Q$ and postcomposition in $I$ commute with this formula on every $a\otimes t$. Quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat $Q$'s induce tensor quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (compare through a K-flat $P$ as in Step 4). They induce Hom quasi-isomorphisms into $I$ by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]; the resulting $J$'s are K-injective over $B$ by Step 3. Quasi-isomorphisms of $C$ and of K-injective $I$'s likewise induce the required Hom quasi-isomorphisms by that lemma. Consequently the commuting chain-level squares remain commuting after inverting those maps. Every morphism of a derived category is a composite of images of complex maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, by the localization description [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; hence these squares give independence of resolutions and naturality on the derived categories.

Taking $H^0$ and applying [lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local] on the one-point sites over $B$ and $S$ gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(X,J_E(V))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E),V).$$
Thus $F_E(X)=U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E)$ is left adjoint to $J_E$. The identity of $J_E(V)$ is sent under this bijection to evaluation: its representative is $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(Q,I)\otimes_B Q\to I$, $h\otimes e\mapsto h(e)$. This complex computes $F_E(J_E(V))$ by the argument in Step 4, since $Q$ is K-flat. Therefore the counit is precisely derived evaluation. The inverse currying formula sends the identity of $F_E(X)$ to the unit $x\mapsto(e\mapsto x\otimes e)$ (followed by a K-injective resolution in the target). The two triangular identities reduce on these representatives to evaluating these two formulas, giving $x\otimes e$ and $h(e)$ respectively.

source.place: Tag 09LT, lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint, with unit and counit from the chain formulas of Tag 09LN

proof.text: For any ring map $K\to S$, the $K$-action is obtained by restricting the displayed $S$-actions. The equality $\theta(sf)(a\otimes e)=s f(a)(e)=s\theta(f)(a\otimes e)$ proves scalar compatibility. The balancing, differential, unit, and evaluation formulas above remain the very same formulas after restriction. Restriction is exact since kernels, images, and cohomology have the same underlying abelian groups, so it takes every comparison quasi-isomorphism used above to a quasi-isomorphism. It therefore takes the isomorphism and its unit/counit compatibilities to the corresponding equalities in $D(K)$, by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This means restriction of the resulting objects and maps, not replacement of $R\operatorname{Hom}_S$ by $R\operatorname{Hom}_K$. Only $Q$ was required to be K-flat over $B$, and only $I$ K-injective over $S$; no boundedness, perfectness, or flatness of $B$ over $S$ entered.
